sources.title: Moons of Mars
sources.text: The two moons of Mars are Phobos and Deimos. Galileo Galilei, as a hidden report about him having observed two bumps on the sides of Saturn (later discovered to be its rings), used the anagram "smaismrmilmepoetaleumibunenugttauiras" for "Altissimum planetam tergeminum observavi" ("I have observed the most distant planet to have a triple form"), Johannes Kepler had misinterpreted it to mean "Salve umbistineum geminatum Martia proles" (Hello, furious twins, sons of Mars).
